title: Indian IT Stocks Hit Three-Year Low as OpenAI Venture Spooks Investors
excerpt: Nifty IT crashes 3.6% after OpenAI announces $4 billion DeployCo, raising existential questions for India's outsourcing giants
body:
India's information technology sector suffered its worst single-day rout in over a year on Monday, with the Nifty IT index plunging 3.6% to a three-year low. The trigger was not earnings or a client loss but something more existential: OpenAI's announcement of DeployCo, a $4 billion AI-native services venture designed to deploy artificial intelligence directly into enterprise workflows.

**The AI Threat Materializes**

For two years, Indian IT executives have insisted that generative AI would create more work than it destroyed, expanding budgets for digital transformation rather than cannibalizing legacy outsourcing contracts. Monday's market reaction suggested investors are no longer buying that narrative. Tata Consultancy Services fell 3.2%, Infosys dropped 3.5%, and Persistent Systems led the decline at over 5%. The Nifty IT index is now down roughly 18% from its 2024 peak.

The concern is straightforward. If AI-native firms can handle enterprise deployment, migration, and integration — the bread and butter of Indian IT services — why would a Fortune 500 company pay for thousands of engineers in Bangalore? HSBC analysts warned in a note that global AI spending could increasingly crowd out budgets previously earmarked for traditional IT services, particularly in application maintenance and testing.

**Compounding Pressures**

The AI scare did not arrive in isolation. Rising crude oil prices, a weakening rupee (which paradoxically helps IT exporters but signals broader economic stress), and uncertainty around US interest rates all contributed to Monday's selloff. Fourth-quarter earnings from top-tier firms had already disappointed, with both TCS and Infosys guiding cautiously on fiscal 2027 revenue growth. Weak discretionary spending by US and European clients — India's primary markets — added to the gloom.

**What It Means for Indian-Americans in Tech**

The selloff carries personal stakes for the hundreds of thousands of Indian-Americans working in or adjacent to the IT services ecosystem. Many hold stock in Indian IT firms through employee plans or family portfolios. More broadly, the AI disruption thesis threatens the very outsourcing model that powered decades of Indian immigration to the US — the pipeline from IIT to Infosys to an H-1B visa to a Silicon Valley career. If that model erodes, the downstream effects on visa demand, remittance flows, and India's tech employment could be significant.

**What to Watch**

Infosys and Wipro report updated guidance this quarter. Investors will parse every word on AI's impact on deal pipelines. If the majors cannot articulate a credible AI-native strategy by mid-2026, the selloff may be just the beginning.
nri_angle: Indian-Americans working in IT services or holding Indian tech stocks face direct exposure. The AI disruption threatens the outsourcing model that powered decades of H-1B immigration and career paths from Indian engineering colleges to US tech corridors.
author: Diaspora Desk
